entries.proposition: DESIGN: open-label stepped-wedge cluster quasi-randomised trial across Ontario paramedic services, each site serving as its own control, with a two-year retrospective lookback and a prospective control period.
entries.snippet: The PRIME Trial is a prospective, multi-centre, pragmatic, two-arm, open-label, stepped-wedge cluster quasi-randomized controlled trial (SW-CRCT).

entries.proposition: POPULATION: children from 1 day to under 18 years with out-of-hospital arrest, so neonates and infants are included; trauma excluded; drowning and hanging included.
entries.snippet: The trial will include children aged 1 day to <18 years who experience an OHCA during the study period

entries.proposition: DOSE: the intramuscular dose is set at up to 10 times the matched IV dose (Table 1: 0.3 mg for 3 to under 5 kg up to 3 mg from 30 kg); the Discussion says 5 to 10 times, an inconsistency of range between two sections.
entries.snippet: In our dosing schedule, we recommend the IM epinephrine dose be up to 10 times higher than the corresponding IV dose for a child of equivalent weight

entries.proposition: DOSE DOUBLING: the authors state the IM peak may coincide with the IV or IO dose, so a child could receive up to double the recommended dose at one time.
entries.snippet: the patient could potentially receive up to double the recommended dose of epinephrine at one time

entries.proposition: SAFETY REASONING: the authors cite a trial of ten-fold epinephrine in paediatric in-hospital arrest as showing no benefit but a trend towards harm, then conclude from data on shorter dosing intervals that the risk of a double dose is minimal; the first paragraph of the Discussion relies on anaphylaxis safety data for a different dose and setting.
entries.snippet: These data suggest that there is minimal risk of harm associated with administering a double dose of epinephrine.

entries.proposition: The safety statement for the trial rests on anaphylaxis practice: no criteria for discontinuing, and no pre-defined stopping rules in the interim analyses.
entries.snippet: There are no pre-defined stopping rules for this trial.

entries.proposition: PRIMARY OUTCOME: time to return of circulation analysed only in patients who achieve it (no censored data), described as an intermediate outcome strongly associated with survival; the adult review read in this batch shows return of circulation moving without a neurological gain.
entries.snippet: will include only patients who achieved ROSC (i.e., there will be no censored data)

entries.proposition: SAMPLE: 86 patients who achieve circulation (43 per arm) to detect an 8-minute difference, scaled to 288 patients at about 30 percent return of circulation, with a cluster size of 3 and an intracluster correlation of 1 percent; control data include two years of historical records.
entries.snippet: we require a sample size of N = 86 patients (n = 43 per group) who achieve ROSC to have 80% probability of detecting a difference in time to ROSC of 8 min or greater

entries.proposition: STATUS: as of 30 December 2024, 139 patients were recruited, 3 in the intervention group, 25 prospective controls and 111 retrospective controls; the protocol version is dated December 2025, so the status paragraph is a year older than the version.
entries.snippet: As of December 30, 2024, we have recruited a total of 139 patients: 3 in the intervention group, 25 in the prospective control group, and 111 in the retrospective control group.

entries.proposition: Figure 3 (SPIRIT schedule): footnotes state hospital-based outcomes will only be collected for patients admitted to the lead hospital, whereas the secondary outcomes include survival to discharge and neurological status after discharge across all sites.

entries.proposition: Figure 1 flow: control arm IV or IO epinephrine immediately (advanced paramedic scope); intervention arm IM epinephrine first (advanced or primary paramedics) then IV or IO immediately after, then every 3 to 5 minutes.
